transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-2025-11-05-acme-poc-8421
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Kim (Redwood SE), Derek Lawson (Acme Head of ML), Priya Shah (Acme Security Lead), Carlos Medina (Acme DevOps), Sana Reddy (Acme PM)

Summary:
- Scoping a 2-week POC focused on data handling and benchmarks for Acme Health patient-facing summarization workload.
- Primary concerns: PII handling, logging/redaction, prompt storage, retention settings, and ingress path (VPC vs secure upload).
- Success criteria: baseline latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics for redaction/accuracy.
- Next steps and action items assigned; Redwood to send SOC2/KMS docs and benchmark harness.

Topics: PII redaction; retention & prompt storage; logging & audit; VPC/networking; benchmarks (latency/throughput/quality); timeline and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — Maya Patel, AE at Redwood. we also have Ethan Kim, our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Derek (Acme): Doing good, thanks. i'm Derek, head of ML at Acme Health. we've got Priya on security and Carlos on infra.
[00:18] Priya (Acme): hi all. main thing for us is patient PII, retention policies, and making sure the logs don't keep sensitive prompt text.
[00:28] Ethan (Redwood SE): Totally understood. today we want to align on the POC scope: data handling, success criteria, and the benchmark plan. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with a baseline run and then a tuning window.
[00:40] Derek: Sounds good. quick context — the workload is patient visit summarization for a subset of clinical notes. about 1000 requests/day for the POC, each request ~400 tokens in prompt, expect ~200 tokens response average. latency target for us is 95th perc < 400ms ideally.
[00:57] Maya: great, that's helpful. on the PII front, Priya, can you describe what you consider PII and what must never be stored?
[01:05] Priya: names, MRNs, DOB, full addresses, phone numbers. we also have indirect identifiers that could re-identify, like rare conditions combined with zip codes — those need handling. retention policy: maximum 30 days for any raw prompts with PHI unless it's explicitly redacted. audit logs ok but need to be redacted or tokenized.
[01:25] Ethan: ok. Redwood offers multiple options: (1) do client-side redaction before sending, (2) use our redaction plugin at ingress which scrubs known fields, (3) run in Private deployment where prompts never leave the VPC. each has tradeoffs for accuracy and complexity.
[01:45] Carlos: For the POC we prefer hosted but with VPC peering — basically private network ingress. we can't do full on-prem for the pilot. is that supported?
[01:54] Maya: yes, we can do VPC peering for Dedicated or Private, for hosted we have a secure upload option and private endpoints. for a short pilot we commonly do a dedicated reserved slot with VPC peering to keep data plane private.
[02:10] Derek: What about logging — we need request/response logs for debugging but want prompts redacted. can Redwood redact automatically?
[02:18] Ethan: We can configure logging to store only metadata (request ids, timing, model used) and either (a) store full payloads encrypted with KMS and TTL/retention, or (b) store redacted payloads where PII fields are replaced with tokens. we also support redaction hooks so you can send us rules to apply before storage.
[02:36] Priya: Do you do deterministic tokenization so we can map back for debugging? we need an audit trail but not raw PHI.
[02:42] Ethan: yes, we have deterministic hashing with salt under customer-managed KMS keys. that means you can map hashed id back if you control the key. by default we use Redwood-managed KMS but the POC can use your KMS for stronger guarantees.
[02:56] Sana (Acme PM): timeline question — 2-week POC, what are the checkpoints?
[03:01] Maya: week 0 - data handoff and redaction rules, week 1 - baseline benchmark (latency/throughput) + quality eval, week 2 - tuning and final pass, deliver SLO report. we'll also run a privacy check to ensure logs/retention meet your policy.
[03:16] Derek: benchmark specifics — we want RPS up to 5 rps, peak concurrency of ~10, and measure 50/95/99 latencies and tokens/sec. also need cost estimate per 1M tokens.
[03:28] Ethan: for that workload size we'll emulate with our harness. recommended test vectors: 200 prompts representative of real variance, include long context, and edge cases with redaction triggers.
[03:40] Priya: about prompt storage — there's a compliance concern that prompts can contain PHI. do you offer ephemeral prompts (no storage) mode?
[03:47] Maya: yes, we support no-persist mode where prompts are processed in-memory and not written to logs or disk, however that limits debugging. often customers do ephemeral for PHI and send a hashed version for instrumentation.
[03:59] Carlos: network detail — if we do VPC peering what is required from our side?
[04:05] Ethan: we'll provide an allowlist of IPs and specific peering instructions; we'll need a couple of firewall rules and a small NAT. we can also do an s3 presigned upload flow if peering isn't possible.
[04:15] Derek: security compliance — do you have SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[04:19] Maya: yes — SOC2 Type II, ISO certs in our pack. I'll share the artifacts after the call.
[04:24] Priya: encryption at rest — we need CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys). is that supported?
[04:28] Ethan: yes, CMEK for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can enable KMS integration so you manage keys for stored artifacts.
[04:35] Derek: what about prompt storage for prompt engineering— we may want to save prompts for training finetune later but need an opt-in. can Redwood segregate that?
[04:44] Ethan: we support per-customer retention policies and per-route configs. you can mark routes as non-persistent or persistent. persistent storage can be limited to a separate bucket with restricted access.
[04:55] Maya: another point: caching and KV cache — to reduce cost and latency we can enable prefix caching but that requires storing prompts/keys. we can restrict caching to non-PHI fields.
[05:07] Priya: That's important. We cannot cache raw PHI. if caching requires storing patient identifiers that's a no-go.
[05:13] Ethan: understood — caching can be applied to sanitized prompt keys only. we can also encrypt cache entries.
[05:20] Derek: success criteria recap — for POC: 95th percentile latency under 400ms, throughput of 5 rps sustained, minimal cost delta from our target (we gave a budget of $X per 1M tokens), and redaction must remove all PHI with false-negative rate < 0.5% on sample set.
[05:40] Maya: yes, please confirm the cost target in an email — we'll scope hardware and reserved capacity accordingly.
[05:46] Sana: who will be our primary contact during the POC for infra questions?
[05:50] Carlos: that's me. I'll own the VPC peering and firewall rules.
[05:53] Ethan: great. on quality metrics we'll run a small eval harness — we'll calculate precision/recall for redaction and an n-gram ROUGE/F1 for summarization quality against golden summaries.
[06:05] Priya: about metrics retention — we can keep only aggregated metrics for 12 months, but raw logs must be purged within 30 days unless otherwise approved.
[06:15] Maya: we'll honor that. Redwood's retention settings are configurable per account/route and we can set a 30-day TTL on raw payloads for the POC.
[06:24] Derek: are transcripts editable? sometimes the firefly export... (laugh) I mean will we be able to remove specific stored prompts after the fact?
[06:31] Ethan: yes, we have a delete API and can do bulk deletes by id or by time range. for extra compliance we can also provide certificate of deletion for PII removal operations.
[06:41] Derek: lovely. a potential blocker is training data leakage — if Redwood uses aggregated telemetry to improve models, will our prompts be used?
[06:49] Maya: by default Redwood does not use customer prompts to train shared models. for Hosted we have an opt-in policy for using data to improve models; for Dedicated/Private there is no training usage. we'll include that in the SOW.
[07:01] Priya: how about function/tool calling logs and tool outputs — those may have PHI too. same retention rules?
[07:07] Ethan: yes; function calls are treated as payload and follow same retention and redaction policies. we can mask tool outputs as well.
[07:15] Sana: on benchmarks — we want results with both quantized and FP16 model variants, to compare latency and cost. can you run both?
[07:23] Ethan: absolutely. we'll run the benchmark across our recommended model variants and report latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll include p95/p99 and tail latency.
[07:32] Derek: for the POC data handoff we'll send a redacted sample of 500 notes and a mapping file with hashed ids. Priya will attach the redaction rules.
[07:40] Priya: correct. and we'll want to review the retention TTL settings before any tests.
[07:45] Maya: noted. we'll also include a test for ephemeral/no-persist mode to see how much observability we lose vs the privacy gain.
[07:53] Carlos: a quick question on authentication — we need SSO for the console and RBAC so only certain folks can view logs. supported?
[07:58] Ethan: yes, we support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC. we can create project-level roles and audit trails for console access.
[08:07] Derek: any gotchas on data egress — if we do VPC peering will logs still be accessible by Redwood ops?
[08:13] Ethan: ops access can be disabled; we can also restrict access to a small set of Redwood service engineers with just-in-time escalation for incidents and full audit logs when that happens.
[08:25] Maya: ok time check — we have about 40 minutes left, we should align on deliverables and timeline.
[08:30] Derek: fine. deliverables: SOW with POC objectives, SOC2 + certs, benchmark harness, and a runbook for data handoff.
[08:39] Maya: Redwood will produce the SOW and share SOC2 docs by Friday. We'll also deliver the benchmark harness and ask Acme to provide the sample dataset and redaction rules.
[08:48] Priya: one more technical nit — when you do deterministic hashing with CMEK, can we rotate keys without losing ability to map old hashes?
[08:56] Ethan: rotation will change hashes unless you keep the old key to re-hash or maintain a key-rotation table. best practice is to rotate and retain previous key versions for mapping, or use a keyed HMAC where you can version. we'll include recommendations.
[09:10] Derek: for success criteria, add an acceptance test where we run 200 real-ish prompts and redaction passes at 99% recall, and summarization quality above our baseline F1 by at least 2 points.
[09:20] Maya: will do. any competitors you're evaluating?
[09:23] Derek: we're still talking to OpenAI and Google Vertex — mostly to compare latency/cost and data controls.
[09:28] Maya: understood. Redwood's differentiator here is per-route retention and customer-managed KMS for the POC.
[09:35] Carlos: ok last infra question — how long to stand up the dedicated slot for the POC?
[09:40] Ethan: we can provision a dedicated pool in 48-72 hours once the SOW is signed. VPC peering usually takes 1-2 business days to configure from customer's side.
[09:50] Maya: great. quick recap of next steps: Maya to send SOC2 and SOW; Ethan to send benchmark harness and test vectors; Priya to send redaction rules and sample; Carlos to coordinate network; Acme to confirm cost target in email.
[10:05] Derek: sounds good. let's schedule a kickoff for next Monday to start baseline runs.
[10:10] Maya: i'll send a calendar invite after the call. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
